overall.verdict: Low Interaction Risk — Minor Notes Only
overall.summary: You are taking metformin for diabetes and lisinopril for blood pressure. When used together they can make the blood‑sugar‑lowering effect of metformin a little stronger, which may cause mild low blood sugar. Watch for symptoms and ask your doctor or pharmacist how to monitor safely.

drugs.boxed_warning: BOXED WARNING WARNING: LACTIC ACIDOSIS Postmarketing cases of metformin-associated lactic acidosis have resulted in death, hypothermia, hypotension, and resistant bradyarrhythmias. The onset of metformin­ associated lactic acidosis is often subtle, accompanied only by nonspecific symptoms such as malaise, myalgias, respiratory distress, somnolence, and abdominal pain. label_hits.text: 7.2 Antidiabetics Concomitant administration of lisinopril and antidiabetic medicines (insulins, oral hypoglycemic agents) may cause an increased blood-glucose-lowering effect with risk of hypoglycemia.

explanation.why: Lisinopril can increase the effect of antidiabetic medicines like metformin, so your blood sugar may drop more than expected.
explanation.timing: The interaction can happen at any time, especially after starting or changing doses; check your blood sugar regularly and let your doctor know if you notice changes.
